proofs.full_local_argument: Put alpha=(epsilon/L2)^(1/2)>0 and beta=epsilon alpha=epsilon^(3/2)/sqrt(L2)>0. For bounded-below C² g define f(x)=(g(x0+alpha x)−g(x0))/beta. Then f(0)=0, inf f=(inf g−g(x0))/beta, and f(0)−inf f=(g(x0)−inf g)/beta<=Delta/beta=T. The chain rule gives gradient f(x)=alpha/beta gradient g(x0+alpha x)=gradient g(x0+alpha x)/epsilon, and Hessian f(x)=alpha²/beta Hessian g(x0+alpha x)=alpha/epsilon Hessian g(x0+alpha x). For x,y, the Hessian difference norm is at most (alpha²/beta)L2 alpha||x−y||=(L2 alpha²/epsilon)||x−y||=||x−y||. Thus f is normalized and the output thresholds correspond exactly. For the lower-bound simulation, take any f in F_d(T), a public real c (choose c=0), and define g(z)=c+beta f((z−x0)/alpha). This g is C² and bounded below, has gap beta[f(0)−inf f]<=beta T=Delta, and Lip(Hessian g)<=beta/alpha³=epsilon/alpha²=L2. Given an unnormalized algorithm query z, query f at x=(z−x0)/alpha of the SAME type. Return value c+beta f(x) and gradient beta/alpha gradient f(x)=epsilon gradient f(x); for a rich query also return Hessian beta/alpha² Hessian f(x)=(epsilon/alpha) Hessian f(x). Each ordinary query costs exactly one ordinary query and each rich query exactly one rich query, without cross-charge. No initialization query is needed: g(x0)=c+beta f(0) need not be computed in advance because each returned value uses the current response f(x). Induction over the full transcript with the same seed shows that replies, adaptive choices and stopping events match those on this fixed g. Measurability, finite termination on legal inputs, input-independent advice and separate pathwise caps are preserved. Counterfactual histories can enforce the same query caps, and any finite internal cutoff used by the normalized proof is removed there under the legal input law. Map any output z, queried or unqueried, to x=(z−x0)/alpha. The identity gradient g(z)=epsilon gradient f(x) makes success events and probabilities identical. Therefore an unnormalized algorithm satisfying its per-input guarantee would satisfy the normalized guarantee for every f with exactly the same G,H caps. Apply the normalized envelope in its T,d,h regime to obtain c min(T d^(1/3),T^(3/2)/sqrt(h+1)). Substituting T=Delta sqrt(L2)/epsilon^(3/2) gives the stated first term and T^(3/2)=Delta^(3/2)L2^(3/4)/epsilon^(9/4), giving the second term. No step establishes an additional global gradient-Lipschitz or Hessian-norm bound.

assumptions: Ordinary queries at arbitrary exact-real z return (g(z),gradient g(z)); rich queries return (g(z),gradient g(z),Hessian g(z)). Rich calls count only toward H and ordinary calls only toward G.

Policies, choices and outputs are measurable with an input-independent private seed. Internal computation is free and terminates in a measurable finite number of steps on every legal input, with no uniform running-time bound; finite parameter-dependent input-independent advice is permitted. Both caps hold on every execution and are enforced on counterfactual histories by stopping before an excess query.
The additive value g(x0) is not assumed observed for free. In the lower-bound simulation choose a public offset c and use g(z)=c+beta f((z−x0)/alpha), without an initialization query.
No precision, radius, span, gradient-Lipschitz or Hessian-norm bound is imposed.
statement.conclusion: Q_unnorm^* >= c min{Delta sqrt(L2) d^(1/3)/epsilon^(3/2), Delta^(3/2) L2^(3/4)/(epsilon^(9/4) sqrt(h+1))}. The scaling preserves d, G and H separately and maps the normalized gradient threshold one exactly to the original threshold epsilon.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For public x0 in R^d and Delta,L2,epsilon>0, let G_d(Delta,L2;x0) consist of bounded-below C² functions g:R^d->R with g(x0)−inf g<=Delta and Lip(Hessian g)<=L2. Put alpha=sqrt(epsilon/L2), beta=epsilon alpha and T=Delta/beta. Normalize f(x)=[g(x0+alpha x)−g(x0)]/beta. Q_unnorm^*(h;d,Delta,L2,epsilon) is the least hard ordinary cap achieving ||gradient g(z)||<=epsilon with probability >=2/3 on every such g, with at most h rich calls and the same measurable adaptive policy convention as the normalized model.
statement.parameter_domains: T=Delta sqrt(L2)/epsilon^(3/2)>=T_*; integer d>=C log(2+T); integer h>=1 and h+1<=a0 T, with C,c,T_*,a0 from the normalized envelope.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every positive Delta,L2,epsilon and public x0, the deterministic inverse construction sends every normalized legal f to an unnormalized legal g with gap <=Delta. An algorithm working for every unnormalized g would simulate on this subclass using the same private seed, preserving the success event and both caps. Constants are the absolute constants of the normalized envelope.
